colors/PaperColor.vim is copied unmodified from that commit. This is the
PaperColor theme itself. It is vendored as a *reference*, not as a scheme
source: it is a Vim theme with no usable ANSI mapping of its own (see
vendor/papercolor-terminal-app/SOURCE.txt for why).

What it is for: the shipped PaperColor packs are decoded from the
Terminal.app port in vendor/papercolor-terminal-app, and
assertPortMatchesUpstreamPalette in tools/external-scheme-sources.ts checks
every one of the port's 16 slots against this file's own color00..color15
for the matching variant. The port turns out to be exactly
`ANSI slot N = colorNN`, so that check passes today and would fail the build
the moment the port drifted from the theme it claims to be.

That is what makes a third-party port acceptable here: its values are not
taken on trust, they are verified against upstream at build time.
